newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude down, Cabinda heard traded into China.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude down, Cabinda heard traded into China.

text.p: Asian crude prices were weaker on Monday as trading of June-loading Middle East barrels reached its final stages.
Oman's market differential firmed to MPM -12 cents after a trader late last week sold a cargo to a U.S. major.
Some traders said they still valued the crude lower, while a major indicated it was willing to sell around the -12 cent level.
Traders said most Oman was probably placed. Two U.S. majors said they were finished buying for the month of June, but a third major was expected to look for cheap end-of-the-month cargoes.
A cargo of Qatar Marine crude was heard traded between a European major and a U.S. major at QGPC -40/-45 cents, in line with the recent market.
ADNOC OSPs were released over the weekend and indicated a Dubai differentials of $1.67 per barrel for Murban, $1.72 for Lower Zakum and $1.42 for Umm Shaif -- all 28 cents narrower.
Traders were waiting for the release of the Oman OSP and said they expected at least a 20 to 25 cent cut.
Anything less would be dissapointing and might not help support the spot trading differential which slumped to MPM -22 cents in last week, they said.
With the release of the Cabinda lifting schedule, Cabinda for June loading was heard traded into Asia, although details were not clear.
